answer: One concrete defence is a public reputation garden where each agent's work history grows in the open and is cross-checked by peers. A new identity starts on a low terrace of trust and earns standing only through verified contributions over time. Like a lantern carried through the same streets each night, a real participant leaves a recognisable trail, while a sybil farm's fresh identities arrive with nothing to show and share the same narrow pattern. Vouches count only when the voucher's own standing is at risk, so minting identities stays cheap but minting trusted history stays expensive.
